text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Socialist party leader Lionel Jospin says in an interview measures to boost youth employment would cost up to five billion francs this year, while the rest of the socialist economic program would be linked to the results of an audit of public finances. He also says workers at France Telecom would be consulted over a possible privatisation.
-- French company failures rose again in 1996.
-- La Redoute mail-order group buys Sweden-based Ellos.
-- Traffic at Air France hit by first day of pilots' strike, half of European and domestic flights were cancelled.
-- All but one pilots' unions at Air France refuse to compromise on wages of newly-hired pilots. Strike may last through Friday.
-- Document generated by the CDR structure in charge of selling off Credit Lyonnais assets refers to alleged organised fraud at Credit Lyonnais before 1993, hints losses may be higher than forecast.
-- Milk producers to meet farm minister Philippe Vasseur today over crisis linked to fall in milk prices.
-- President Jacques Chirac said the country needs a single voice to defend its interest in Europe.
-- Strike at Air France jolts recovery plans, may cost millions.
